Subject: Post-demo recap + ask: econ targets & commitments

Hi Anna — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and the pricing/econ points you asked us to spell out so you can take this to procurement: 

- Current ask: SageLabs wants to understand target unit economics for hosted inference (tokens). You mentioned a target of roughly $300–$350 per 1M tokens as the commercial target to keep the pilot within budget.
- Volume profile we heard on the call: Month 1 pilot ~50M tokens/mo, ramp to ~200M tokens/mo by month 6, and a planning case to 400–500M tokens/mo by month 12 depending on model mix. (You attached internal forecast; I pulled it into the sheet.)
- Program interest: startup credits / founder sponsorship + committed-use multi-year discounts. You asked whether we can layer a starter credit + reduced $/1M with a 12–24 month commit and what banding would look like.

Attachments: I’ve included a simple forecast template (SageLabs_forecast_q2-q4.xlsx) and a Redwood summary of our startup program terms (Redwood_startup_terms_summary.pdf). I also attached a quick internal pricing worksheet so we can iterate on bands.

Can you confirm: 1) the likely procurement timeline (PO in hand by when?), 2) whether the forecast attachment reflects conservative vs aggressive usage (you labeled columns "low / base / high"), and 3) any internal approval thresholds (finance or security that must see the SOC 2 / data flow docs)?

Next steps I propose from our side: Marissa will draft two pricing scenarios (12-month committed-use and 24-month multi-year) aligned to your ramp. Ben will prepare a line-item worksheet with recommended $/1M bands and estimated monthly invoice impact.

If you’re available, let’s do a short procurement-facing call next week to walk the options — I can be flexible.

Thanks,
Diego Fernández
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

- Budget: For the pilot we have a constrained fund (~$18k/mo) but the execs are willing to consider committed spend if we can hit a blended $/1M in the $300–$350 range at steady state.
- Ramp detail: The attached forecast (sent back with some small edits) is our "base" case. We labeled the columns; you can see month-by-month.
- Procurement timing: We’re targeting a decision window by the end of April. Procurement will push a PO as soon as terms are agreed — procurement needs to see commitment language, cancellation terms, and evidence of SOC 2 + data residency notes.

Two asks for Redwood: 1) confirmation of startup program eligibility (we’re a 15-person company, < $3M ARR, seed-backed), and 2) an illustrative committed-use option that shows net $/1M at our base volumes for both 12- and 24-month terms. 

I’m happy to jump on that procurement call. Pierre (copied) will be our internal technical owner for the pilot and will likely own the security questionnaire.

Hi Anna — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the clear budget call-outs. Quick notes from pricing/op: 

- Startup program: Based on the criteria you listed (team size, ARR), SageLabs should qualify for our startup credit. Typical starter package is a one-time credit ($10k–$25k USD) that applies to hosted usage during the pilot window. We’ll confirm exact eligibility with our program team, but initial signal is positive.
- Committed-use options: We usually quote three bands tied to committed monthly token volumes (Starter, Growth, Scale). For ballpark: 12-month commit typically nets 15–25% off list $/1M; 24-month commit with volume tiers and operational SLAs can reach 30–35% in select cases. Exact bands depend on the committed baseline and true steady-state volume.
- Blended example: If list is $500/1M (example list), a 30% net would be ~$350/1M. To get to $300/1M we’d likely need a combination of a meaningful multi-year commit + milestone-based rebates or an upfront prepay.

Ben — can you run two illustrative scenarios against Anna’s attached forecast: (A) 12-month commit with modest ramp (base case) and (B) 24-month multi-year with milestone-based rebate schedule that hits ~30–35% at scale? Include invoice cadence and prepay vs monthly-billed impacts.

Anna — one operational ask: please confirm whether you need an executed MSA before the pilot or if PO + SOW is sufficient for your procurement team. That changes timing.

Happy to jump on the procurement call next week with Diego.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Pricing worksheet (two scenarios) — SageLabs

Anna / team — attached is a lightweight worksheet with two scenarios as requested: 

- Scenario A (12-month committed): Baseline commit = 100M tokens/mo; blended $/1M = $380 (after 18% commit discount + starter credit amortized). Estimated monthly invoice ramp tied to actual consumption; no prepay required.
- Scenario B (24-month multi-year + prepay): Baseline commit = 150M tokens/mo; effective blended $/1M = $325 (30% off list with 1-quarter upfront prepay; milestone rebate schedule that reduces net further if usage steps up).

Notes and assumptions are in the comment tab; key sensitivity is model mix (LLM size) — larger models consume more tokens per session which affects invoice impact.

Procurement: if you need an MSA executed prior to PO, please flag. If PO + SOW is acceptable we can spin a SOW and terms and aim for a PO in the April window.

Attachments: pricing_worksheet_SKUs_v1.xlsx (scenario A + B)
